label: August 1880
atlas_dek: The episodes of anti-Black violence reported in August 1880 from our dossiers, our earliest month, placed on 1910 county lines and by month (some July events were first reported in August). Hover for a short summary; select a dot to read the account in the sidebar. Drafts: no entry has had human review.
reader_intro:
Dossiers for 60 episodes of anti-Black violence reported in August 1880, our earliest month. They come from the 78 located events in the August 1880 table, which includes July events first reported in August, and from an extra check for attacks by a single person (below). We did not write dossiers for 14 events that were plainly out of scope from the table alone (white victims, legal executions, no race given, duplicates, election violence recalled from earlier years). Searches covered August papers, plus September papers for more on known episodes.

Seven of the 67 dossiers are set aside. Two are duplicates folded into another record: the Gibson Station report of the hanging of Bill Peters and Long Monday in the Creek Nation, and a second record of the posse killing of Harry Wheeler at Lacroix’s Ferry, Louisiana. In five, no report gives anyone’s race: J. C. Corlew at Moberly, Missouri; Charley Norton at Kokomo, Colorado; the masked men who drove newly arrived miners from Coalton, Ohio; Thomas Watkins at Fort Scott, Kansas; and Waldron, taken from the sheriff and killed at Sunnyside, Georgia.

Attacks by one person: our definition covers violence by groups and by people acting with public authority, so an attack by a single private person is normally left out, even when the motive is plainly racial. For August 1880 we tested that rule. An extra agent pass read every August article cluster for one-person attacks on Black people, and each one whose attacker was not reported Black got a dossier. These entries say that one attacker acted alone. Whether they belong in the count is still open.

Police violence is kept generously: men shot while fleeing or while a warrant was served are included. Only gunfights over a crime in progress are set aside. Where no report gives the victim’s race, the entry says so.

Method: a research agent (Sonnet) searched the papers. A write-up agent (Opus) wrote the dossier with keyed citations, and a code check confirmed every quote and citation against the article text. For 1880 our sources hold no Black press, so every account rests on white papers; clippings are shown as page images where we could place them on the scan, otherwise as text.

Drafts: no entry has had human review.
